decision_reason: INV-CODEC-TB-003 (trailing-bytes check precedes verify_digest_match) is a structural ordering invariant; the cheapest sufficient verifier is a structural diff review plus call-site inspection. No automated verifier (Kani/Verus/Flux) expresses call-ordering as cheaply. INV-CODEC-TB-006 (diagnostic-code wiring parity) is also a mechanical review: the new match arm must exist in diagnostic_code() and symbolic_code() for the new variant.

INV-CODEC-TB-001 (decoder returns Err(TrailingBytes { trailing }) iff bytes.len() > payload_end) is locked directly by test inversion: rename decode_ignores_trailing_bytes_beyond_payload to decode_rejects_trailing_bytes_after_payload (0xFF 0xFE 0xFD 3-byte fixture), and add decode_envelope_only_rejects_trailing_payload (4-byte fixture). INV-CODEC-TB-005 (trailing > 0) is locked by the trailing_bytes_variant_and_fields trio at error_tests.rs. Cargo test is the cheapest verifier because the assertions are direct variant matches on a 3-byte fixture; Kani would be over-spec.

INV-CODEC-TB-002 (Ok only if bytes.len() == payload_end) and INV-CODEC-TB-010 (round-trip unchanged) are universal claims over the encode-then-decode pipeline. Property-based random JournalEvent values encoded then decoded give the strongest cheap coverage that the new check never fires a false-positive on well-formed inputs. Proptest shrinking makes any failure actionable.

INV-CODEC-TB-003 (trailing check precedes verify_digest_match) is the strongest claim about step ordering. Kani H6 in kani_postcard_envelope_wire.rs stubs verify_digest_match as a counted call and asserts the count is zero for any input with bytes.len() > payload_end. This is the only verifier that mechanically proves call-ordering rather than relying on review. Kani's symbolic execution is bounded because the existing H5 harness already exhausts the same header/payload shape with #[kani::unwind(4)]; H6 inherits that.

INV-CODEC-TB-007 (Verus PS-003 bridge enumerates Err(SpecJournalError::TrailingBytes { trailing: u32 })) is mandatory for GOD RULE 2 compliance: adding a new JournalError variant without updating the bridge breaks scripts/check-verus-production-binding.sh and scripts/check-production-inner-drift.sh. The binding mechanism is WEAK_MIRROR (production_inner/vb_vzcuf_PS_003_production.rs is already a verbatim mirror of crates/vb_storage/src/codec/mod.rs:1-100 with drift-gate enforcement). Direct STRONG #[path] binding is impossible because the production codec transitively reaches postcard / blake3 / crc32c, which are not Verus-modelable in single-file verus --crate-type=lib.

HOSTILE-INPUT-001 requires a fuzzer oracle: build a valid record, append N (0..=8) trailing junk bytes, assert Err(TrailingBytes) when N > 0 and Ok when N == 0. Proptest cannot prove the same claim against arbitrary attacker-shaped input at the same depth; Kani cannot express 'attacker' as cheaply. Cargo-fuzz is the rust-contract skill's primary verifier for hostile input.

vb_storage codec functions are pure parsers over &[u8]; no concurrent memory ordering, no lock-free structures, no channel interleavings, no Send/Sync shared-state across the decode boundary. decode_record_payload has no Arc/Mutex/atomic in its body or its callees (verify_digest_match, decode_record_header). The crate is single-threaded synchronous. Loom would not expose new bugs beyond what Kani already proves about byte-level inputs.
